html:
The Estallido social, or social outburst, was a wave of mass protests in Chile that began on 18 October 2019, after a rise in Santiago metro fares. It grew into a revolt against inequality.

Students began by jumping the metro turnstiles. Within days, riots burned metro stations, and millions marched in Santiago and other cities. Their anger was at low pensions, costly health and education, and the market model of the Chicago Boys. Police and soldiers killed dozens, and hundreds suffered eye injuries from rubber bullets.

The parties agreed to a vote on a new constitution, and in 2020 nearly four in five voters backed replacing the one of Pinochet. But voters rejected a first draft in 2022 and a second in 2023. Chile kept its old charter, with the protests' questions unanswered.
sum: The Estallido social, or social outburst, was a wave of mass protests in Chile that began on 18 October 2019, after a rise in Santiago metro fares. It grew into a revolt against inequality.
